adoptionSource: On 2026-11-24 the project operator selected “Adopt the plan and budgets” for the nine same-machine scenarios, eight hours, 1,000 calls, one authorized repair and three attempts without progress. The decision covers initial binding. Execution and the final boundary require separate decisions.
amendmentPolicy: An adopted change to scope, scenarios or acceptance conditions requires a canonical superseding decision and the repository signed amendment path.

cleanup: Independently inspect the post-run inventory and preserve redacted receipts, including failed/blocked checks.
expectedEffects: Runner creates isolated test resources, builds once with locked manifests as a phase boundary prerequisite, and records each scenario and its independent negative control.
receipts: One receipt per typed packet command with source/fixture hashes, observations, assertions, cleanup and outcome.
boundaryPacket.requiredApprovals: Owner adoption and normal local B4 boundary authorization. After an authorized repair rerun only affected entries and controls.
stopConditions: Restore local state on failure or missing prerequisites. An unmet oracle is FAIL; unavailable isolation or dependencies are BLOCKED. No unreported skips.

budgets.exhaustion: Checkpoint and report BLOCKED with outstanding mandatory cases; never promote incomplete evidence.
budgets.tokenFallback: Owner adopted the time and tool-call ceilings in place of an explicit token budget.

scenarioMatrix.name: Live bidirectional updates with optional local Companion

negativeControl.expectedRejection: Neither subscribed session shows the unrelated event. Removing the live update from the evidence makes the independent oracle fail.
negativeControl.input: Leave a second, unrelated project open and write a different command there.

oracle.comparator: Require both original PIDs and overlapping lifetimes, the exact event IDs, verified signatures, project and next work in both directions. Each observed effect occurs once per cursor, including the event written while the watcher was stopped. Reject a preexisting event from before the barrier.
oracle.expectedTruthSource: Preassigned distinct command IDs, signed device public keys, start barriers, monotonic timestamps and the initial audit.
oracle.observation: Both original session processes and their preexisting watchers observe the other session’s post-barrier signed record/clear traffic before either session exits. The shared-Companion variant has direct server-side command and stream evidence; the standalone variant has a provably absent endpoint. A restarted observer resumes across the interruption.

scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: In both variants start two independent long-lived sessions and establish both prometheus kbd watch subscriptions before either writes. A invokes prometheus kbd blocker record with a fresh nonce; B observes that event and invokes prometheus kbd blocker clear for the same blocker. A observes the reply. Repeat against one shared local Companion. Check status and audit independently; exercise watcher restart against a new write.

oracle.observation: Interactive fallback identifies its source; reconnect closes watch gaps. Explicit receiver checks fail closed. Claim races have one authoritative result and replay is idempotent.

negativeControl.expectedRejection: An A-only receipt cannot satisfy receiver application. Conflicting reuse is rejected and B’s count stays unchanged.
negativeControl.input: Hold back the signed push after A has committed and collect both A’s receipt and B’s direct audit; replay same request ID with different payload.

oracle.comparator: Bind both live session and Companion PIDs, enrolled keys and socket paths to the captured command request, response and recipient stream. Compare B’s direct socket and live SSE observations to A’s source event ID, command ID, signature and hash. Require B’s frontier and waypoint to match. Same push ID/bytes returns same receipt and exactly one event.
oracle.expectedTruthSource: Original signed command bytes, known A and B endpoints, all initial frontiers, expected command ID; verify signatures with enrolled fixture public keys.
oracle.observation: B changes only after the explicit signed request; audit, stream, frontier and waypoint match and remain in place after restart.

oracle.comparator: Cover a backlog representative of Full’s observed document and one above the actual encoded limit. Check every transmitted frame is within bounds and all intended events eventually arrive exactly once after interruption. Compare B’s waypoint with the verified revision and frontier following recovery.
oracle.expectedTruthSource: Deterministic signed backlog generator and independently enumerated command IDs/digests, byte lengths before transmission, B’s preserved pre-write projection and ledger.
oracle.observation: A representative backlog converges without exceeding negotiated bounds. A stale projection is observable and regeneration restores it from durable signed history.

oracle.comparator: Match each baseline check to a per-profile expected/observed result. Unfiltered doctor exits zero without unexpected failures or warnings. Demonstrate intentional profile exclusions accurately, run every applicable full-profile check, reject blanket disabling and maintain real standalone sign/read, continuity and disposable-service results.

oracle.observation: The nine recorded failures and listing warning are individually resolved, including skills-only expectations. Full native required services respond, and all previously passing integration controls still pass.

oracle.comparator: Independently compare baseline IDs and per-item dispositions with fresh unfiltered results. Require zero invalid items/strict failures, no filter or severity downgrade, zero unexplained loss, and semantic preservation evidenced by the canonical project records.

oracle.observation: All 158 baseline Full items have identifiable and valid successors; all 130 recorded failures are resolved and all new/current items pass strict validation. Companion’s previously passing workspace change stays valid.
